`./index.html` is written and is the only file in the working directory. Both self-check vectors match, and the strategy averages about 46.6 waves on 80 seeds of my own. I tested the page in WebKit, not Chrome, because no Chrome was available on this machine.

## Self-check vectors
- **Vector A:** score 25.38, fall tick 1035, 166 entries, hash `82a5353d` — matches.
- **Vector B:** score 10.93, fall tick 457, 48 entries, hash `2e8858d7` — matches.
- Both were checked from the script text extracted out of the shipped file, and again inside the loaded page (`BENCH_REPORT.selfCheck` is computed at load).

## Strategy
- **Design:** `plan()` carries a private copy of the rules and forecasts every enemy it already knows about (board, current wave, previewed wave, plus one synthetic wave to soak fire). While the forecast shows no leak it banks gold for interest; otherwise it buys the build or upgrade with the best forecast leak reduction per gold.
- **Layout:** slot roles came from hill-climbing on 32 training seeds: a lance at the gate, cannons along the road, flak by the air lane, one bolt near the keep.
- **Targeting:** `target()` picks the splash centre with the most effective damage, weighting menders ×6 and runners ×2; the lance and bolt shoot menders first.
- **Measured score:** mean 46.59 waves over 80 seeds on the shipped text (two blocks of 40: 46.66 and 46.51; worst seed 43.95, best 48.93). A further 32 held-out seeds on the same configuration averaged 46.75. For reference, the all-bolts baseline of vector A holds 25.38.
- **Seed 42:** 47.53 waves, falls at tick 1921, so the collapse is visible at about 96 s in the replay. Seed 42 was never used for tuning.
- **Safety:** about 0.3–0.9 s of CPU per full game under JavaScriptCore. Every action it emitted in the checked games was valid and affordable, and every target id was a real candidate.
- **Robustness to the reference engine:** the strategy does not read the ambiguous view fields (`speed`, `slowed`, slot/turret `x`/`y`, `range`, `spent`, enemy `x`/`y`). Scrambling them leaves the seed-42 game hash unchanged.

## Implemented
Everything in the spec is implemented:
- **Board and units:** board, road, air lane, pads, keep, five turret types with tier pips, seven enemy types with health bars.
- **Combat visuals:** all shot, kill, heal, split and build/upgrade/sell effects; leak chunks and red flash; fall collapse with shockwave, shake and desaturation.
- **HUD, audio, controls:** the in-canvas HUD, synthesized audio, and the five-state playback machine.

## Simplified
- The keep has 10 chunks, one per base HP, so a leak of 2 or 3 damage knocks off 2 or 3 chunks rather than one.
- After the fall, enemies freeze at the positions of the last completed tick.
- Enemies get a small fixed per-id visual offset so stacked ones stay distinguishable.

## Browser testing
**Verified in WebKit (an offscreen macOS WKWebView):**
- The finished file loads with no console errors.
- Screenshots at 1280×650 and 1920×1080 look right across the timeline: start, early, mid, late, the fall, and after desaturation.
- A scripted run through the controls behaved as specified: countdown 3/2/1, pause and resume, speed pills, re-fire hold, scrubbing, end state, restart.
- 60 fps (vsync-capped) at 1920×1080 with device pixel ratio 2 through the densest waves. That is the number in `measuredFps`.

**Not verified:**
- Chrome itself, and frame rate on a mid-range discrete GPU.
- How the audio sounds. The code ran without errors, but nothing was listened to.
- A hash match against your reference engine beyond the two vectors. Tier-3 turrets, custom targeting and base HP going below zero on the final leak (I log the raw value) are not covered by them.
